purpose: Teach: キャッチボール/プーチン/チャングム/ビクトリア/ヨコ/東海道/ゴア/ナビゲーション

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと息子がキャッチボールを楽しんだ
lines.en: You know, Gran, when your father was young, he used to play catch with your grandfather.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Voice gentle and slightly distant, as if looking back through time. Measured pace. The affection sits quietly underneath, not performed.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、プーチン政権の動向をご覧になってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, dear — and do you remember how your grandfather used to follow the news about Putin's government?
lines.style: Warm and present, lightly teasing. A knowing smile in the voice. Gentle pivot away from his memory, steering gently back to him with affection and a touch of playful deflection.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがチャングムの韓ドラを観てらした
lines.en: Gran, I remember when your father was young — he loved watching that Korean drama, Jangum, so much.
lines.style: Returning to the memory. Wistful again, but with a touch of quiet amusement at the specific detail. Unhurried. The voice carries fondness for the fact itself, not just the past.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ビクトリア女王の伝記を愛読されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And your grandfather, he was such a devoted reader of biography — Victoria's life particularly, if I recall.
lines.style: Matching his rhythm now, but with gentle certainty. A woman who knows her husband's habits well. Tender and matter-of-fact at once. No sentimentality, just accuracy and warmth.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがヨコの繋がりを大事にされた
lines.en: When your father was young, he treasured those horizontal connections with people — he understood that deeply.
lines.style: The voice slows. This memory carries weight. Deliberate. The wistfulness deepens into something more reflective. Breathing space before the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、東海道新幹線開業を喜ばれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather was so pleased when the Tokaido Shinkansen opened, do you remember? He talked about it for years.
lines.style: Warm certainty again, with a hint of gentle knowing. She's bringing him back to his own moment in history. The affection is in the accuracy of the memory, not the tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがゴア元副大統領の演説を聴かれた
lines.en: When your father was young, he attended a speech by Al Gore, the former vice president. He was quite moved by it.
lines.style: Quieter now. The wistfulness is deepening toward something more settled. Slower pace. A memory that sits peacefully, without needing embellishment.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ナビゲーションを使いこなしてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And your grandfather, he took to navigation technology so naturally, didn't he? Picked it up right away.
lines.style: Gentle, closing warmth. Her voice softens further. A final tender observation about him, offered with quiet affection. The kind of small, true detail that means everything.
